# JMAP/IMAP/CalDAV client setup

The web client is one way to use Envoir — everything it does is also reachable from ordinary mail,
calendar, and contacts apps, because a node exposes one MOTE store through several standard
protocol front-ends. This page is for pointing an existing tool (Thunderbird, Apple Mail/Calendar/
Contacts, a phone's built-in apps, DAVx⁵) at Envoir instead of using the web client.

## What's served where

| Protocol | Served by | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| **JMAP** (RFC 8620/8621) | The node, natively (`ENVOIR_JMAP=1`) | The modern sync surface — mail, and (via extension kinds) calendar/contacts |
| **IMAP** (RFC 9051/3501) | The optional [gateway](#running-the-gateway) (`GATEWAY_IMAP_ENABLE`) | Legacy mail clients |
| **POP3** (RFC 1939) | The gateway (`GATEWAY_POP3_ENABLE`) | Simple download-and-delete legacy clients |
| **SMTP-submission** (RFC 6409) | The gateway (`GATEWAY_SUBMISSION_ENABLE`) | Sending mail from a legacy client |
| **CalDAV** (RFC 4791) | `crates/dmtap-mail`'s compatibility server | Apple Calendar, Thunderbird, DAVx⁵ |
| **CardDAV** (RFC 6352) | `crates/dmtap-mail`'s compatibility server | Apple Contacts, Thunderbird, DAVx⁵ |

Every one of these authenticates with an **app-password** bound to your identity — never your
identity keypair directly (spec §8.2). Mint one from [Settings & devices](#settings#node-connection-leaving-the-demo-behind)
on a real node.

## Autodiscovery

If your domain publishes the right records, most clients configure themselves automatically:

- **SRV records** for generic autodiscovery.
- **Thunderbird autoconfig** — the standard `autoconfig.<domain>` lookup.
- **Apple `.mobileconfig`** — a downloadable profile for iOS/macOS Mail/Calendar/Contacts.
- **Microsoft Autodiscover** — both classic POX and v2 JSON, for Outlook.

If autodiscovery finds your domain, you'll only ever be asked for your address and app-password.

## Manual setup — IMAP/SMTP (Thunderbird, most desktop clients)

1. Add a new account, choose manual/advanced setup.
2. **Incoming (IMAP)** — host is your gateway's address, port `1143` (gateway defaults; an
   operator may run TLS on a different port), username is your full address, password is your
   app-password.
3. **Outgoing (SMTP submission)** — same host, port `1587`, same credentials.
4. For POP3 instead of IMAP, use port `1110`.

These ports are the gateway's own defaults — see [Running the gateway](#running-the-gateway) if
you're standing one up yourself, or ask your operator for their actual host/ports.

## Manual setup — CalDAV/CardDAV (Apple Calendar/Contacts, DAVx⁵)

1. Add a new CalDAV (or CardDAV) account.
2. Server address is your node's compatibility-server URL.
3. Username is your full address, password is your app-password.
4. The server projects your Envoir calendar/contacts as ordinary iCalendar/vCard collections — no
   Envoir-specific client behavior required on the other end.

## What you gain and lose versus the web client

Everything routed through these compatibility surfaces is still stored as real, end-to-end
encrypted MOTEs on your node — a legacy client reading over IMAP or CalDAV doesn't see any less
privacy at rest. What you lose is Envoir-specific UI: the [MOTE inspector](#mail#inspecting-a-message--the-mote-inspector),
[transport-path provenance graph](#transport-traceability), [safety-number](#identity#safety-numbers-verifying-a-contacts-key)
verification affordances, and the honest tier/send-note language in
[Compose](#compose#what-the-honest-send-note-means) are all web-client concepts a generic IMAP
or CalDAV client has no way to render.

## Deferred protocol surfaces

Real TLS termination and a couple of niche extensions (cross-server CATENATE URLFETCH, exotic
nested-message BODYSTRUCTURE envelopes, JMAP push transport) are explicitly deferred as transport
concerns — see [`kotva-mail/README.md`](https://github.com/vul-os/kotva/blob/main/crates/kotva-mail/README.md) (now in the
sibling [vul-os/kotva](https://github.com/vul-os/kotva) repo as `kotva-mail`) for the exact
capability matrix.
